 Kenenisa Bekele set to race Valencia Half Marathon 
 The Ethiopian great returns to racing just weeks after withdrawing from the Berlin Marathon with an Achilles injury
 Keeley Milne Published October 18, 2026 
 -->
 Katie Chan/WC
 Ethiopian distance-running legend Kenenisa Bekele will race Spain’s Valencia Half Marathon on Oct. 25, according to the official start list released Friday. The 44-year-old, whose career achievements include three Olympic gold medals and a world masters marathon record, could be chasing another masters best in Valencia.
 Bekele has a half-marathon PB of 1:00:22, set at London’s Big Half in 2020. He will line up alongside a deep field that includes Spain’s Rodrigue Kwizera , who has a PB of 58:16, Ethiopia’s Jemal Yimer (58:33), Tadese Worku (58:47) and Kenya’s Daniel Ebenyo (59:04).
 The complete elite fields of Valencia #HalfMarathon 🇪🇸 (25 Oct.) are now available:
https://t.co/I9lpE6QIf5
And look who has recovered from his pre-Berlin injury: Kenenisa Bekele 🇪🇹
@MedioMaratonVLC
 — Marathon News (@Marathon_N) October 17, 2026 
 Bekele was also scheduled to run the Berlin Marathon in September, but withdrew three days before the race due to a left Achilles tendon injury. His entry in Valencia comes just over a month after that withdrawal.
 A long career at the top
 At the 2004 Athens Olympics, Bekele won gold in the 10,000m, followed by gold in both the 5,000m and 10,000m at Beijing 2008. He also owns five world championship titles on the track and spent years dominating international cross-country racing. After making his marathon debut in 2014, he went on to become the second-fastest marathoner in history at the time, running 2:01:41 at the 2019 Berlin Marathon, just two seconds shy of Eliud Kipchoge ‘s then-world record.
 In 2024, Bekele, then 41, finished second at the London Marathon in 2:04:15, breaking his own world masters record for runners aged 40–44. He had set the previous record of 2:04:19 just five months earlier, at the 2023 Valencia Marathon. He also represented Ethiopia at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he finished 39th.
 Valencia: fast and flat
 Valencia has become one of the world’s fastest half marathons, with both men’s and women’s world records set on its course in recent years. Ethiopia’s Yomif Kejelcha ran 57:30 there in 2024, while compatriot Letesenbet Gidey set the women’s world record of 1:02:52 in 2021.
 The 2025 edition saw Kejelcha successfully defend his title in 58:02, while Kenya’s Agnes Ngetich won the women’s race in 1:03:08, the third-fastest women’s half marathon in history at the time.
 This year’s race, the 35th edition, takes place on Sunday, Oct. 25. To learn more about the Valencia Half Marathon, check out the official website, here .
